cards.explanation: The reason He gives is that He is the LORD their God. The verse says, “For I am the LORD your God.” (Leviticus 26:1) No long list and no fine print, friends. Who He is is the reason on the page.

The answer is True. Right after the idols, the LORD says, “You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.” (Leviticus 26:2) Two more commands, back to back. He's building a list, and I'm taking notes with my mustache.

The first thing on the list is rains in their season. The LORD says, “I will give you rains in their season…” (Leviticus 26:4) Then the land yields its produce and the trees bear fruit. The rain comes first and the rest follows.

The answer is True! The LORD says, “you will have your fill of food to eat and will dwell securely in your land.” (Leviticus 26:5) That means full plates and a safe place to enjoy them. Both blessings come in the same breath.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will rid the land of dangerous animals…” (Leviticus 26:6) He also says they'll lie down with nothing to fear. Fewer things lurking means better sleep for everybody.

Five Israelites will pursue a hundred. The LORD says, “Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand…” (Leviticus 26:8) Five against a hundred is already wild, friends. Then the numbers keep climbing.

The two blanks are old and new. The verse says, “You will still be eating the old supply of grain…” (Leviticus 26:10) The old grain isn't even finished yet. That's the kind of problem I'd like to have. The LORD says they'll need to clear it out “…to make room for the new.” (Leviticus 26:10) The new harvest shows up before the old one is gone, and plenty is crowding the storeroom.

The answer is True, and this might be the best blessing on the list. The LORD says, “And I will make My dwelling place among you, and My soul will not despise you.” (Leviticus 26:11) Full fields are great. Having Him close is greater.

The answer is Egypt. The LORD says He is the one “…who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians.” (Leviticus 26:13) He points back to what He already did for them, friends. He adds that He broke the bars of their yoke.

The answer is walk in uprightness. The LORD says, “I broke the bars of your yoke and enabled you to walk in uprightness.” (Leviticus 26:13) The bars are broken, and then they can walk upright. He gave them more than freedom from the yoke.

The answer is enemies. The LORD says, “You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.” (Leviticus 26:16) They do the planting, and someone else gets the harvest. That's a hard thing to watch.

The answer is that they will flee when no one pursues them. The LORD says, “…you will flee when no one pursues you.” (Leviticus 26:17) Earlier they were the ones chasing, and now they're running from nobody. The blessing flipped all the way over, friends.
The answer is their stubborn pride. The LORD says, “I will break down your stubborn pride…” (Leviticus 26:19) Pride is the first thing He names here. Then He goes on to the sky and the land.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “…your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.” (Leviticus 26:20) There's no smaller harvest in this verse. The fields give nothing.

The answer is wild animals. The LORD says, “I will send wild animals against you to rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers…” (Leviticus 26:22) The roads end up desolate too. This is a heavy verse, friends.

The answer is False. The wild animals will rob the Israelites of their children, “…destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers…” (Leviticus 26:22) Their livestock is on the list. It's a hard verse to sit with.

The answer is His discipline. The LORD says, “…if in spite of these things you do not accept My discipline, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me…” (Leviticus 26:23) They keep walking in hostility instead of accepting it. And He's still speaking, friends.

The answer is plague. The LORD says, “Though you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you…” (Leviticus 26:25) Walls won't keep it out. They end up delivered into the hand of the enemy.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…you will eat but not be satisfied.” (Leviticus 26:26) Ten women bake the bread in a single oven, and it's doled out by weight. They do eat, and it still isn't enough. I think this one is heavy, friends.

The answer is on the remains of their idols. The LORD says, “…heap your lifeless bodies on the lifeless remains of your idols…” (Leviticus 26:30) I think this one hurts to read. It sits right next to the high places and the incense altars.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will reduce your cities to rubble and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.” (Leviticus 26:31) So what the verse gives us is the refusal, not the aroma, friends.

The answer is Sabbaths. The LORD says, “…the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate…” (Leviticus 26:34) The land gets its Sabbaths while the people are in the land of their enemies. Verse 35 says it will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when they lived in it.

The land gets the rest it missed while Israel lived there. The LORD says, “…the land will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when you lived in it.” (Leviticus 26:35) The rest it missed is the rest it gets, friends.

The answer is the sound of a windblown leaf. The LORD says, “…even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight.” (Leviticus 26:36) Not a trumpet and not an army, just a leaf. I think this one is heavy.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “You will perish among the nations…” and the survivors “…will waste away in their iniquity and will decay in the sins of their fathers.” (Leviticus 26:38-39) It's a hard stretch of the sermon, friends.

The answer is His covenant with their forefathers. The LORD says, “…I will remember My covenant with Jacob and My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.” (Leviticus 26:42) Three names, and He remembers each covenant. After a long hard stretch, this is the turn, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…they will pay the penalty for their iniquity, because they rejected My ordinances and abhorred My statutes.” (Leviticus 26:43) The text gives that as the reason. It's a sober line.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “…I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.” (Leviticus 26:44) His covenant stays standing, even there, friends.

The answer is Sinai. The verse says these are the laws the LORD established “…between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.” (Leviticus 26:46) Moses is the one the LORD sent to bring His people out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10). That's the closing line of the whole sermon, friends.
